title: Exchange Online: sending from aliases is GA
summary: The Exchange team says Sending from Aliases is generally available: users can send and reply from any proxy address on their mailbox in Outlook on the web, Outlook for Windows and Mac, and Outlook mobile, after a tenant-wide switch (Set-OrganizationConfig -SendFromAliasEnabled $True, or EAC → Settings → Mail flow) that can take up to 60 minutes to apply. To stop a whole domain from sending, such as the onmicrosoft.com domain, mark it receive-only with Set-AcceptedDomain -SendingFromDomainDisabled. Known gaps per Microsoft: address-based rules and journaling can miss alias traffic, message trace needs the alias in the query, shared mailboxes only work in OWA via Open another mailbox, and in hybrid, auto-replies can come from the mail.onmicrosoft.com routing address. The post was first published on 7 October and updated on 18 November.
why: Users can now pick any domain on their mailbox as the visible sender. That means every accepted domain they hold an alias in must be ready to send: SPF, DKIM and DMARC alignment for that domain, and transport rules, DLP and journaling that match on the alias, not just the primary address. There is no per-mailbox control, so the decision is tenant-wide.
todo: Do now: check Get-OrganizationConfig | fl SendFromAliasEnabled — commenters report it was already on in some tenants without an admin action.

For each accepted domain that appears in user aliases, confirm SPF includes Exchange Online, DKIM signing is enabled and DMARC is aligned; set domains that should never send to receive-only with Set-AcceptedDomain -SendingFromDomainDisabled $true.
Update mail flow rules, DLP, journaling and message-trace runbooks to match aliases. Wait if you are hybrid with centralized mail flow until you have tested auto-replies.
